issues.problem: R4-23 incomplete: OpenCode strict mode still passes --auto (auto-approve), in both the NI and interactive argv. The new strict-by-default for outside-project work dirs therefore gives no protection on OpenCode, and Pi has no permission controls at all, while the opencode/pi SKILL.md Permission-mode rows promise 'strict never adds bypass flags'. silver-multi-ai-task/SKILL.md:81 itself lists 'OpenCode runs without --auto' as the safe configuration.
issues.evidence: PATH=<stub opencode>:$PATH bash -c 'source scripts/lib/agent-host-exec.sh; agent_host_build_argv opencode non-interactive /w PROMPT strict' -> 'run --dir /w -m opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 --auto PROMPT'; interactive strict -> '/w -m opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 --auto --prompt PROMPT'. Adapter: args=(run --dir ... --auto) unconditionally, then '+=(--auto)' again for permissive.
issues.suggested_fix: Add --auto only when permission_mode/mode is permissive (host-exec and adapter, NI and TUI), with argv assertions next to the Codex ones. For Pi, either refuse --mode strict with an honest 'strict unsupported on Pi' error or state plainly in the skill that Pi has no strict mode.

issues.problem: Coverage exclusion hides shipped production code: scripts/lib/agent-adapters/* (fnmatch '*' also crosses '/', so any future file under that directory is excluded too). scope.json's own _comment says 'never exclude a file only because it is hard to test'. These files are now on the default /sb:agent-* path in installed packages, and about half of them already runs under stub CLIs.
issues.evidence: Re-reporting this review's scoped run with the exclusion removed (sbcov.SCOPE_FILE patched in a sandbox copy of scope.json): claude.sh 1/103 stmts, codex.sh 100/175, opencode.sh 64/84, pi.sh 42/72 => 207/434 (47.7%). The Claude adapter, the default path for /sb:agent-claude, is essentially unexecuted by the delegate tests (they use fake --sb-root adapters).
issues.suggested_fix: Remove the exclusion. Cover the NI/exec/argv/env paths with stub CLIs, as test-agent-codex-adapter-trust.sh already does for Codex exec. If some genuinely live-only TUI/expect blocks remain, move them into separately named files and exclude those by exact path with a reason, or add audited line entries to known-limits.json. Do not ship tests/live in the Codex package instead: that reverses the R13-13 payload-shrink decision.

issues.problem: The test-harness transcript default became production behaviour. Every Codex TUI delegation (the default without --use-exec) writes the prompt plus the full session transcript to ${SB_ROOT}/tests/live/agents/codex/transcripts/ (latest.jsonl, latest.meta.json and 4 rotated archives). In an installed package SB_ROOT is the plugin cache, which CLAUDE.md calls a read-only build artifact. The files are unredacted, use the default umask and outlive the task and the project. This is new exposure created by R10b-05 and conflicts with R4-31's goal.
issues.evidence: agent_transcript_dir: printf '%s\n' "${CODEX_TRANSCRIPT_DIR:-${SB_ROOT}/tests/live/agents/codex/transcripts}"; codex_capture_transcript does mkdir -p plus cp/python copy and runs after every TUI invoke (line 399); no redaction, no chmod. The author's report lists this as open item (4), 'unchanged'.
issues.suggested_fix: Default the transcript dir to the task dir (.planning/agent-codex/<task-id>/), or to a 0700 TMPDIR dir removed with the run, and keep the SB_ROOT/tests path only when SB_LIVE_* test isolation is active. Create the files 0600 and pass them through agent_redact.py --redact-file. Add a test that a delegate run from a scripts-only package writes nothing under SB_ROOT.

issues.problem: R10b-06 part (b) is still reproducible in another form: the brief scanner hard-rejects ordinary auth-feature briefs that contain code. Assignment values that are identifiers, dotted references or calls pass the length-16/entropy-3.5 test. The rejection has no override, and the error does not say which pattern matched, so the user cannot act on it.
issues.evidence: printf '%s' '<line>' | python3 scripts/lib/agent_redact.py --scan -> rc=1 'assignment' for: 'client_secret: settings.GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET', 'const password = req.body.passwordConfirmation', 'secret=getSecretFromVaultClient()', 'private_key: loadPrivateKeyFromDisk(path)', 'Use secret: process.env.SESSION_SECRET for cookie signing'. agent_delegate_resolve_prompt then returns 2: 'ERROR: brief contains secret patterns — remove credentials before launch'.
issues.suggested_fix: In _looks_random, treat code-shaped values as non-secrets: dotted identifier chains, values with '(' or ')', env references (process.env., os.environ, getenv), and pure [A-Za-z_] identifiers without digits; require character-class mixing such as digits plus letters, or base64/hex shape. Name the matched kind in the error message. Add these honest samples to the accepted table in test_agent_redact.py and the behaviour test.

issues.problem: The 'inside the current project' test is a path-prefix test against CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, then the git toplevel, then $PWD. A separate repository cloned inside the project, and anything under a non-repo cwd/CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (a session started in $HOME or in a parent folder), default to permissive.
issues.evidence: cwd=proj, work dir proj/vendor/third (its own git init) -> 'permissive'; CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$HOME (not a repo), work dir $HOME/src/clone -> 'permissive'. Sibling dir and an outside linked worktree -> 'strict' as intended.
issues.suggested_fix: Require the work dir's own git toplevel (or git-common-dir) to equal the project's; when the project dir is not a git repo, only the exact dir is 'the project'. Print one stderr line naming the chosen default mode, so a strict downgrade (for example for an outside sibling worktree, where Codex workspace-write cannot write the main repo's .git) is visible.

issues.problem: Ephemeral folder trust (hasTrustDialogAccepted) is seeded for every Claude delegation, including strict ones into a directory outside the project. That is the trust-prompt bypass R4-23 asked to disable in strict mode (for interactive/PTY runs the repo's project hooks and settings load without a prompt).
issues.evidence: agent_claude_prepare_lightweight_config_dir always calls agent_claude_seed_folder_trust; no mode check; probe log '[agent-claude] seeded folder trust for <work> in <tmp>/agent-claude-config-*/.claude.json' on a default (strict-eligible) run.
issues.suggested_fix: Skip seeding when the effective mode is strict, or document why it is safe.

issues.problem: The quota retry gating is weaker than its message implies. The classifier runs over the whole output, so test text still matches. The fingerprint (HEAD + porcelain names + diff HEAD) does not see edits to pre-existing untracked files, gitignored files (.env, build/, node_modules) or writes outside the work dir. A read-only verification task whose failing test prints 'expected status 429' is re-run up to 5 times with 60 s sleeps.
issues.evidence: is_quota_error true for 'expected status 429, got 200', 'FAIL: rate limiter should return Too Many Requests', 'quota exceeded test passed', 'implementing rate limit exceeded handler'. retry_decision returns RETRY after 'echo more >> notes.txt' (existing untracked), 'echo x > build/o' (ignored) and a write to ../outside.txt.
issues.suggested_fix: Classify only lines that look like CLI/provider errors (stderr, JSON error objects, lines beginning with Error/API Error), and include untracked file contents (git ls-files -o --exclude-standard -z | xargs -0 git hash-object) in the fingerprint. Document ignored-file and outside-dir writes as residuals.

issues.problem: The stale lightweight CODEX_HOME sweep removes any of this user's agent-codex-codex-home-* dirs whose directory mtime is older than 120 minutes. A concurrent long-running delegation (interactive idle timeout 3600 s, and appends to existing files do not change the top-level dir mtime) can have its live CODEX_HOME, including auth.json, deleted by a second delegate starting.
issues.suggested_fix: Write the owner PID into the home and sweep only dirs whose PID is dead, or touch the dir periodically.

issues.problem: Opt-in global seeding: os.replace turns a symlinked ~/.claude.json (dotfile managers) into a regular file, and there is no lock against a concurrent Claude write (lost update). R8-15 asked for an flock.
issues.evidence: ln -s real.json ~/.claude.json; SB_AGENT_CLAUDE_SEED_FOLDER_TRUST_GLOBAL=1 ... -> ~/.claude.json is now a 218-byte regular file; real.json unchanged.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve the symlink and write the target (or refuse), and take an flock on a sidecar lock file.

decisions.1_coverage_exclusion: Not acceptable as written. It is shipped code on the default delegation path, scope.json forbids hard-to-test exclusions, the glob is recursive, and about 48% already executes under stubs. Cover the exec/argv/env paths with stub CLIs; isolate any truly live-only TUI code by exact path, or add audited line limits. Do not ship tests/live in the Codex package (payload shrink, R13-13).
decisions.2_strict_default_outside_project: Right direction and documented (CHANGELOG plus the four skills; SB_AGENT_DELEGATE_DEFAULT_MODE and --mode override). Honest in-project delegations, subdirectories, symlinked paths and worktrees under the project stay permissive (probed). Fix the prefix heuristic (nested clones, non-repo project dir), print the chosen default, and note that outside linked worktrees now get Codex workspace-write and Claude acceptEdits. The safety claim is false on OpenCode until --auto is dropped in strict.
decisions.3_quota_retry_gating: Safe and usable. Provider text is required, retries stop in a non-git dir unless --quota-retry, 5-hour windows are never short-retried, and real quota errors normally fail before any tool call, so the tree is unchanged and the retry still happens. Note that --quota-retry now has two meanings (re-enable retries on the pinned-NI fast path, and skip the unchanged-tree check), which the skills should spell out. Tighten the classifier to error lines and add untracked-file content to the fingerprint (minor).
